  *****NOTE FROM THE CITY*****

Doors to the City Council Chamber will open at 1:30 p.m. for Open Session. Please be mindful, however,
that there is limited seating in the City Council Chambers; therefore, the Gladys Waddingham Lecture
Hall (located adjacent to the Main Library) will be opened as an overflow room and will be available for
the public to watch the meeting and to speak.

ALTERNATIVE METHODS
The City provides the following two alternative methods of viewing and listening to the City Council Meeting as a
convenience:

  ¡  On Spectrum Cable Channel 35 with audio and limited video. Please check with your cable provider
  for details.
  ¡  Live online through Facebook Live, with audio and limited video, at
  https://www.facebook.com/cityofinglewood/

The disruption in service of any alternative method does not preclude the City Council or other legislative body
from taking further action on an agenda item.

Submitting Comments Prior to Public Meeting: Members of the public may choose to submit comments
electronically for consideration by the City Council or other City Legislative Body by sending them to the City
Clerk/Secretary at athompson@cityofinglewood.org, and Deputy City Clerk at aallen@cityofinglewood.org. To
ensure distribution to the members of the Legislative Body prior to consideration of the agenda, please submit
comments prior to 8:00 a.m. the day of the meeting, and in the body of the email, please identify the agenda
number or subject matter. Correspondence should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments received
after 8:00 a.m. and prior to the close of the public hearings will be made part of the official public record of the
meeting. Contact the Office of the City Clerk at 310-412-5280 with any questions.

ACCESSIBILITY: If requested, the agenda and backup materials will be made available in appropriate
alternative formats to persons with a disability, as required by Section 202 of the Americans with Disabilities Act of
1990 (42 U.S.C. Sec. 12132), and the federal rules and regulations adopted in implementation thereof. Any
person who requires a disability-related modification or accommodation, or translation services in order to observe
and/or offer public comment may request such reasonable modification, accommodation, or service by contacting
the Office of the City Clerk by telephone at 310-412-5280, FAX at 310-412-5533, One Manchester Boulevard,
First Floor, Inglewood City Hall, Inglewood, CA 90301 or via email to athompson@cityofinglewood.org and
aallen@cityofinglewood.org no later than 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting.

Inglewood, California
  April 4, 2023

  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
  April 4, 2023, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the City
  Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, and Joint Powers
  Authority at the hour of 2:01 p.m.
  The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary/Joint Powers
  Authority Secretary announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman/ Joint Powers Authority Chairman Butts,
  Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing
  Authority Members/ Joint Powers Authority Members
  Dotson, Padilla, Morales, and Faulk; and
  Absent:  None.
  City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/ Joint Powers Authority officials and personnel
  present were as follows:
  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Louis Atwell  Acting City Manager/Acting Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, and Joint Powers
  Authority.

  133  CELEBRATION OF LIFE. Mayor Butts read a Proclamation regarding the Celebration
  of Life for Wayne Spencer.

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman/ Joint Powers Authority Chairman Butts inquired
  if there were any persons present who wished to address the City Council/Successor
  Agency/Housing Authority/ Joint Powers Authority on any item on the Agendas other than
  the Public Hearings.

  Speaker (Name Unknown) commented on Agenda Item Nos. 6, Authorize payment of an
  invoice submitted by the City of Manhattan Beach, and 7, Authorize purchase orders to
  AT&T Services, Inc. and payment authorization of four (4) invoices submitted by FirstNet.

  142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member
  /Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Faulk that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated March
  29, 2023, in the amount of $4,588,835.98, and March 24, 2023, in the amount of
  $5,056,445.46 are hereby allowed, and the City Clerk/Successor Agency
  Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to certify upon said registers
  that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
Ayes:  Council Members/ Successor Agency Members/ Housing Authority Members
  Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor/ Successor Agency Chairman /
  Housing Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes:  None.
 April 4, 2023

301  PUBLIC HEARING HELD – CATEGORICAL EXEMPTION EA-CE-2022-129-
  AFFIRMED; RESOLUTION NO. 23-77 ADOPTED - SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO.
  SP-2022-008 (SELF STORAGE FACILITY AT 937-959 WEST HYDE PARK
  BOULEVARD) WITH APPROPRIATE FINDING AND SUBJECT TO 13
  CONDITIONS. The City Clerk announced the next scheduled matter was a public hearing
  to consider adoption of a resolution approving a certain Special Use Permit request to allow
  an approximately 70,000 square-foot addition to an existing 156,000 square-foot 6-story
  self-storage facility on an approximately 74,000 square-foot, M-1 (Light Manufacturing)
  zoned property at 937-959 West Hyde Park Boulevard, and that notice was given in the
  time, form and manner as required by law, an affidavit was on file, and communications
  were received.

  The City Clerk, Aisha L. Thompson received communications via email from John R.
  Patterson, who supported Special Use Permit No. SP-2022-008.

  Mayor Butts ordered the communications received and filed.

  Louis Atwell, Acting City Manager, presented the staff report dated April 4, 2023.

  Bernard McCrumby, Senior Planner, presented a brief oral report.

  Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present that wished to address the City
  Council on the matter.

  Speaker (Name Unknown) spoke opposing Special Use Permit No. SP-2022-008 and
  questioned the Planning Commission’s decision to deny this project.

  Tom Baden stated that he attended the Planning Commission’s hearing and spoke in
  opposition to Special Use Permit No. SP-2022-008. He stated that the project was on a
  local street with heavy traffic. He also stated people speed through the area and felt  it
  would be an over-improvement. Additionally, he discussed the surprise at the approval of the
  first stage due to the lack of parking, over-improvements, employment, and traffic
  congestion. Finally, he reiterated his opposition to this project.

  Dave Rand spoke in favor of Special Use Permit No. SP-2022-008 stated that it would
  expand the facility next door. He also noted that his client believed there was a need for this
  project. He addressed the low impact on traffic, the community, and parking  congestion.
  Additionally, he added that the project was the best use in terms of disturbances and effects on
  the neighborhood. Furthermore, he addressed the addition of additional  public storage by
  expanding an existing facility that leases successfully. Finally, he requested  the  project's
  approval and agreed with the Planning Staff's conditions of approval.

  Erick Harold spoke in opposition to Special Use Permit No. SP-2022-008 stated that it
  was an eyesore for the community. He noted the existing building reminded him of jail and
  didn’t want it in the community. He also stated that the area was supposed to be high-  tech,
  but the building was a big blob. He addressed a public storage facility on Hyde Park  and the
  land used to store RVs. Finally, he discussed the lack of need for additional  seven-story
  high-rise buildings and the loss of employment.

  Speaker (Name Unknown) spoke in opposition to Special Use Permit No. SP-2022-008
  stated that he lives down the street from the building and that building another one would
  be insane. He also noted that the big white building does not belong on that street in
  Inglewood. He addressed nearby storage facilities and questioned how many storage
  facilities were needed. Finally, he reiterated that another storage facility was not needed.

  Mayor Butts closed the public comment portion at the hour of 2:18 p.m.

  Following discussion, it was moved by Council Member Dotson, and seconded by Council
  Member Morales that the City Council does hereby: 1) Affirm the categorical exemption
  EA-CE-2022-129; and 2) Adopt Resolution No. 23-77 entitled:

  2
 April 4, 2023

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, APPROVING A CERTAIN SPECIAL USE
  PERMIT REQUEST TO ALLOW AN APPROXIMATELY 70,000 SQUARE- FOOT
  ADDITION TO AN EXISTING 156,000 SQUARE- FOOT 6 STORY  SELF-STORAGE,
  M-1 (LIGHT MANUFACTURING) ZONED PROPERTY AT  937-959  WEST  HYDE
  PARK BOULEVARD.

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

142  PUBLIC HEARING HELD – RESOLUTION NO. 23-78 ADOPTED – AMENDING
  THE MASTER FEE SCHEDULE. The City Clerk announced the next scheduled matter

  over-year 8% increase in the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics Consumer Price Index (CPI),

  The City Clerk, Aisha L. Thompson received communications via email from Marvin

  Mayor Butts ordered the communications received and filed.

  Sharon Koike, Assistant Finance Director/CFO presented a brief oral report.

  Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present that wished to address the City
  Council on the matter.

  There was no response.

  Mayor Butts closed the public comment portion at the hour of 2:29 p.m.

  Following discussion, it was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member Padilla that Resolution No. 23-78 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,

  be adopted. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
